nature: Salary
desc: TDS on salary paid by an employer to an employee — government or private.

variants.condition: All employees (State Govt., Union Govt., non-Govt.)

notes: No flat rate — computed on estimated annual taxable salary after all declared deductions/exemptions, spread evenly across the year's pay cycles.
keywords: salary employee employer payroll slab tds on salary

nature: Accumulated PF balance withdrawal (taxable portion)
desc: Premature withdrawal of the taxable part of accumulated EPF balance, if service is under 5 years.
noPan: 20% (Maximum Marginal Rate is not applied here, unlike some other heads)
notes: No TDS if service exceeds 5 years, or transfer is between recognised PF accounts, or withdrawal is due to ill-health/discontinuation of employer's business.
keywords: epf pf provident fund withdrawal premature

nature: Insurance commission
desc: Commission paid to insurance agents for soliciting/procuring insurance business.

variants.condition: Payee is a company or other entity

notes: Rate depends on who receives the commission (the agent), not who pays it.
Cut from 5%/10% to 2%/10% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
keywords: insurance commission agent lic policy

nature: Commission or brokerage (other than insurance, and other than securities brokerage by stock exchange)
desc: Any commission or brokerage paid to a resident, excluding insurance commission (194D) and underwriting commission.
notes: Individual/HUF payers deduct only once their own turnover/receipts cross the specified-person threshold (₹1 crore business / ₹50 lakh profession in the preceding year).
keywords: commission brokerage agent dealer

nature: Rent
desc: Rent paid by a company, firm, or audit-liable individual/HUF for any land, building, furniture, plant or machinery.
notes: Threshold is per payee, aggregated across the year, checked monthly.
A separate, lower-threshold rule (194-IB) applies instead when the tenant is an individual/HUF not liable to tax audit — see that section.
keywords: rent land building furniture office premises landlord machinery equipment plant hire

nature: Rent paid by an individual/HUF not liable to tax audit
desc: Rent on any property paid by an individual or HUF who is not otherwise required to deduct TDS under 194-I (i.e., not liable to tax audit in the preceding year).
noPan: 20% (capped at last month's rent if tenancy ends mid-year)
notes: Rate cut from 5% to 2% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
Applies regardless of turnover — this is the one rent provision with no audit-based exemption for individuals/HUF.
Deducted once a year (or on vacating), not monthly — a single challan-cum-statement (Form 141) suffices.
keywords: rent individual huf tenant landlord flat house not audit

nature: Payment under Joint Development Agreement (JDA), consideration not wholly in kind
desc: Monetary consideration paid by a developer to a landowner under a JDA for development of property.
notes: Applies only to the cash component; consideration given wholly in kind (constructed area) is taxed on transfer of that share, not under this section.
keywords: joint development agreement jda land owner developer

nature: Purchase of immovable property (other than rural agricultural land)
desc: TDS by the buyer of any immovable property on the consideration paid to a resident seller.

variants.threshold: ₹50 lakh (consideration or stamp duty value, whichever higher)

noPan: 20% — the standard rate here, NOT the concessional 5% used for goods purchase/e-commerce
notes: Deducted on the FULL consideration once the ₹50 lakh threshold is crossed — not just the excess.
Where multiple buyers/sellers are involved, the threshold is tested on the aggregate transaction value, not each individual's share.
Deposited via Form 141 within 30 days from month-end of deduction; seller gets a Form 16B-equivalent certificate.
keywords: property purchase flat house immovable builder buyer stamp duty

nature: Income from units of mutual funds
desc: Income (other than capital gains) distributed on mutual fund units to a resident unit holder.
keywords: mutual fund units income distribution
notes: Threshold raised from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 by Budget 2025.

nature: Interest on securities
desc: Interest on debentures, government securities, and other listed/unlisted securities.

variants.threshold: ₹10,000/yr (debentures of a widely-held company); no threshold for most other securities

notes: No TDS on interest on securities held in demat form and listed on a recognised stock exchange, subject to conditions.
No TDS on interest on notified Government securities (e.g. 8% Savings (Taxable) Bonds threshold ₹10,000 applies).
keywords: interest securities debenture bond government security

nature: Interest other than interest on securities (bank/FD/deposit interest)
desc: Interest paid by banks, co-operative societies, post offices and others (not being interest on securities).

variants.condition: Interest from co-operative society or post office deposits

notes: Bank applies the ₹1,00,000 senior-citizen threshold automatically using the age on record — no separate application needed.
Submit Form 121 (replaces 15G/15H) to prevent deduction where total income is below the taxable limit.
No TDS on interest credited to a savings account, or on compensation awarded by a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal below ₹50,000.
keywords: fd interest fixed deposit bank senior citizen co-operative post office

nature: Payments to contractors/sub-contractors
desc: Payment for carrying out any work (including supply of labour) under a contract, by specified persons.

variants.threshold: ₹30,000 single payment, or ₹1,00,000 aggregate in the year

variants.condition: Payee (contractor) is a company, firm or other entity
variants.threshold: ₹30,000 single payment, or ₹1,00,000 aggregate in the year

notes: The 1% vs 2% split depends on who is BEING PAID (the contractor), never on who is paying.

Separate condition on the payer's side: an individual/HUF payer must deduct at all only once their own business turnover exceeded ₹1 crore, or professional receipts exceeded ₹50 lakh, in the preceding year — the 'specified person' test. Below that, no deduction obligation arises regardless of the contractor's status.

Small-transporter exemption continues under Sec 393(4) (old 194C(6)): a transporter owning ≤10 goods carriages during the year, furnishing PAN + declaration, is exempt. Exemption covers only owned carriages, and stops applying (prospectively) once the 11th carriage is added.
keywords: contractor payment individual huf works contract sub-contractor payee transporter

nature: Fees for professional or technical services, royalty, director's fees
desc: Fees for professional services, technical services, royalty, non-compete fees, and any director's remuneration not in the nature of salary.

variants.condition: Fees for technical services / call-centre operations / royalty for sale/distribution/exhibition of films
Professional fees (CA/CS/CMA, legal, medical, engineering, architectural, interior decor, advertising, technical consultancy etc.)
Director's fees / sitting fees (not being salary)

notes: Confusing professional fees (10%) with technical services (2%) is the single most common under-deduction error under this section — audit/CA fees, legal fees and medical fees are 'professional', not 'technical'.
Director's fees apply from the first rupee — the ₹50,000 threshold does not apply to this variant.
keywords: professional fees ca legal medical consultancy audit fee lawyer doctor architect technical services call centre director sitting fees royalty

nature: Dividend
desc: Dividend (including deemed dividend and dividend on preference shares) paid by an Indian company to a resident shareholder.
notes: No TDS if paid to LIC, GIC, another insurer, or to a shareholder who submits a valid Form 121 (income below taxable limit).
keywords: dividend shares preference equity shareholder

nature: Life insurance policy maturity / survival benefit (taxable portion)
desc: Sum received under a life insurance policy (including bonus) that is not exempt under Sec 10(10D).
notes: Deducted on the INCOME COMPONENT (sum received minus premiums paid), not the gross payout.
Cut from 5% to 2% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
keywords: lic maturity life insurance survival benefit policy bonus

nature: Purchase of goods
desc: TDS by a buyer of goods on the value paid/payable to a resident seller.

variants.condition: Buyer's turnover exceeded ₹10 crore in the preceding year
variants.threshold: Value exceeding ₹50 lakh from one seller in the year

notes: Deducted only on the amount exceeding ₹50 lakh, not the full value (unlike 194-IA property purchase).
The overlapping TCS under old Section 206C(1H) was withdrawn from 1 April 2025 — this TDS is now the only compliance point for high-value goods purchase.
keywords: purchase of goods buyer supplier

nature: Business perquisites or benefits (in cash or kind)
desc: Any benefit or perquisite (cash or in kind) arising from business or profession, given to a resident.
notes: Covers free samples, sponsored trips, gift vouchers and similar business perks — deductor must ensure tax is paid even where the benefit is wholly in kind (may require the recipient to pay the tax portion in cash first).
keywords: perquisite benefit in kind business gift freebie sponsored trip

nature: E-commerce operator's payment to a seller
desc: TDS by an e-commerce operator (Amazon, Flipkart, etc.) on gross sale/service value facilitated for a resident seller.
notes: Cut from 1% to 0.1% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
keywords: ecommerce e-commerce amazon flipkart seller marketplace

nature: Transfer of virtual digital asset (crypto / NFT)
desc: Consideration for transfer of a virtual digital asset, deducted by the payer.

variants.condition: Specified person (individual/HUF with no business income, or turnover below tax-audit limits)

noPan: 20% (can also go up to 30% under specific anti-avoidance readings — verify current CBDT guidance)
notes: No set-off of losses on one VDA against gains on another is allowed at the income-tax computation stage — a separate rule from this TDS provision, but relevant to the same transaction.
keywords: crypto cryptocurrency vda virtual digital asset bitcoin nft

nature: Repayment under National Savings Scheme
desc: Amount paid on closure/withdrawal of deposits under the (legacy) National Savings Scheme.
notes: Relevant only to legacy NSS accounts opened before the scheme's discontinuation for new deposits.
keywords: nss national savings scheme deposit withdrawal

nature: Repurchase of units by Mutual Fund / UTI
desc: Formerly covered repurchase of units under Sec 80CCB schemes.
notes: Withdrawn with effect from 1 October 2024. No successor provision under the new Act — listed for reference only, so it isn't mistaken for a still-active section.
keywords: mutual fund repurchase units uti discontinued withdrawn

nature: Commission on sale of lottery tickets
desc: Commission, remuneration or prize paid on stocking, distributing, purchasing or selling lottery tickets.
notes: Cut from 5% to 2% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
Threshold raised from ₹15,000 to ₹20,000 by Budget 2025.
keywords: lottery ticket commission agent seller distributor

nature: Compensation on compulsory acquisition of immovable property
desc: Compensation (including enhanced compensation) paid on compulsory acquisition of immovable property, other than rural agricultural land.
notes: Compensation for compulsory acquisition of agricultural land itself remains exempt from tax and hence from TDS.
Threshold raised from ₹2,50,000 to ₹5,00,000 by Budget 2025.
keywords: compulsory acquisition compensation immovable property land government enhanced

nature: Distribution by a business trust (REIT/InvIT) to unit holders
desc: Interest, rental income, or dividend component distributed by a business trust to its unit holders.

variants.condition: Rental income component — resident unit holder
Dividend component (where SPV opted out of concessional regime) — resident unit holder

notes: Non-resident unit holders are taxed under the Sec 393(2) non-resident table instead, generally at 5% for interest and other specified rates by income type — confirm the exact sub-rate for the income head before deducting.
keywords: business trust reit invit unit holder distribution interest rental dividend

nature: Income from units of an investment fund (Category I/II AIF)
desc: Income (other than exempt business income) paid by an investment fund to its unit holders.
notes: Non-resident unit holders: rate in force under the applicable head, subject to DTAA.
keywords: investment fund aif income unit holder category I II

nature: Income from investment in a securitisation trust
desc: Income paid by a securitisation trust to its investors.
notes: Unified to a flat 10% for all investor types by Budget 2025 — previously 25% (individual/HUF) and 30% (others).
keywords: securitisation trust investment income

nature: Payment by an individual/HUF not otherwise liable to deduct, to contractors/professionals/commission agents
desc: Contract, professional fee, brokerage or commission payments made by an individual/HUF who is below the 194C/194H/194J turnover threshold and so wouldn't otherwise deduct at all.

variants.condition: Individual/HUF payer below the specified-person threshold

notes: Exists specifically to catch high-value contractor/professional/commission payments by individuals/HUFs (e.g. a large home-renovation contract) who fall outside 194C/194H/194J because their own turnover is below the audit threshold.
Cut from 5% to 2% on 1 Oct 2024 — carried forward, not a 2026 change.
keywords: individual huf payment contractor professional commission not liable

nature: TDS by specified bank for senior citizens aged 75+ (ITR-filing exemption)
desc: A facilitation provision, not a separate income head: a specified bank computes and deducts the FULL final tax liability of a senior citizen (75+) whose only income is pension and interest from that same bank, so the senior citizen need not file an ITR at all.

variants.condition: Senior citizen 75+, income limited to pension + interest from the same specified bank
variants.rate: Slab rate (computed by the bank after all eligible deductions)
variants.threshold: No threshold — this is a computation mechanism, not a payment-triggered deduction

notes: Only applies where the senior citizen has furnished a declaration to the bank; if other income exists (rent, capital gains, etc.), this section doesn't apply and normal ITR filing is required.
keywords: senior citizen 75 pension bank itr exemption declaration

nature: Income of a non-resident sportsman or sports association / entertainer
desc: Income from participation in India (match fees, advertisement, contribution of articles) by a non-resident sportsman, sports association, or entertainer.
notes: Plus applicable surcharge and cess. DTAA rate may apply if beneficial, subject to TRC/Form 10F.
keywords: non resident sportsman entertainer foreign athlete association

nature: Interest from an Infrastructure Debt Fund
desc: Interest paid by a notified Infrastructure Debt Fund to a non-resident.
keywords: infrastructure debt fund interest non resident idf

nature: Interest paid by an Indian company/business trust in foreign currency (ECBs, masala bonds)
desc: Interest on borrowings under a loan agreement, or on long-term bonds/rupee-denominated bonds, issued by an Indian company to a non-resident, in foreign currency.

variants.condition: Certain notified long-term bonds/rupee-denominated bonds listed on a recognised stock exchange (incl. IFSC)

notes: Borrowing must be approved by the Central Government and within the specified period to qualify for the concessional rate.
keywords: ecb external commercial borrowing masala bonds foreign currency loan non resident

nature: Interest on rupee-denominated bonds/Government securities paid to FII/QFI
desc: Interest on rupee-denominated bonds of an Indian company or Government securities, paid to a Foreign Institutional Investor or Qualified Foreign Investor.
notes: Concessional rate is time-bound to interest payable up to specified dates notified from time to time — verify the current sunset date before relying on it.
keywords: fii qfi rupee denominated bonds government securities interest

nature: Income from units of a mutual fund/UTI paid to a non-resident
desc: Income (other than capital gains) from mutual fund/UTI units, paid to a non-resident (not being a company) or a foreign company.
keywords: mutual fund uti income non resident units

nature: Income from units of an offshore fund
desc: Income (including long-term capital gains) from units purchased in foreign currency by an offshore fund.
keywords: offshore fund income units non resident

nature: Income from foreign currency bonds or GDRs of an Indian company
desc: Income and long-term capital gains from foreign currency bonds or Global Depository Receipts of an Indian company, purchased in foreign currency.
keywords: gdr global depository receipts foreign currency bonds non resident

nature: Income of Foreign Institutional Investors from securities
desc: Income (other than dividend income and capital gains) from securities, paid to an FII.
notes: Subject to lower DTAA rate where a valid Tax Residency Certificate and Form 10F are on file.
keywords: fii foreign institutional investor securities income

nature: Any other payment to a non-resident (incl. royalty, technical fees, business income)
desc: Catch-all provision: any sum (other than salary) payable to a non-resident or foreign company that is chargeable to tax in India, and not covered by a more specific section above.
noPan: 20% or higher (Sec 397(2) no-PAN rule applies on top of the computed rate)
notes: DTAA rate needs a valid Tax Residency Certificate and Form 10F on file before it can be applied — the lower rate isn't automatic on the strength of a claim alone.
Surcharge and cess apply in addition to the base rate.
Payer must file Form 15CA/15CB (or successor forms under the new Act) before remitting, for most payments in this category.
keywords: foreign payment non resident royalty technical fees dtaa consultant abroad 15ca 15cb

nature: Winnings from lottery, crossword puzzle, card game or other games of gambling/betting
desc: Winnings from lotteries, crosswords, card games and similar games (excluding online games, which fall under 194BA).
notes: Flat rate — no slab benefit or basic exemption applies.
Where winnings are wholly/partly in kind, the distributor must ensure tax is paid before releasing the prize.
keywords: lottery gambling crossword winnings prize card game

nature: Winnings from online games
desc: Net winnings from any online game (including real-money gaming, fantasy sports).
notes: Deducted on NET winnings at the time of withdrawal, and again on the remaining balance at year-end if not already taxed.
No basic exemption — unlike 194B, tax applies from the first rupee of net winnings.
keywords: online game winnings gaming rummy fantasy real money

nature: Winnings from horse races
desc: Winnings from any horse race run on a licensed racecourse.
keywords: horse race winnings betting racecourse

nature: Cash withdrawal from a bank/post office account
desc: TDS on cash withdrawals exceeding specified limits from one or more accounts with a bank, co-operative bank or post office.

variants.condition: Recipient has filed ITR in all of the preceding 3 years
variants.threshold: ₹1 crore/yr from a single payer (₹3 crore/yr for co-operative societies withdrawing for banking business)

variants.condition: Recipient has NOT filed ITR for any of the preceding 3 years
variants.rate: 2% on withdrawals between ₹20 lakh–₹1 crore; 5% above ₹1 crore

notes: 'Co-operative society engaged in banking business' gets the higher ₹3 crore threshold; all other recipients (including individuals) get ₹1 crore.
Government, banks and certain other notified recipients are excluded from this section entirely.
keywords: cash withdrawal bank account individual co-operative non filer itr higher rate

nature: Partner's salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest from a firm/LLP
desc: Any salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest credited/paid by a partnership firm or LLP to its partner.
notes: Applies to every firm and LLP — no turnover or audit threshold exemption.
Triggers on CREDIT to the partner's account, even without any cash payment — a journal entry is enough.
In force since 1 April 2025 (Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024) — this is its second year, not a 2026 introduction.
Pure profit-share distribution to a partner is NOT covered — only these four specific heads are.
keywords: partner salary remuneration commission interest llp firm 194t bonus

nature: Sale of specified goods (liquor, forest produce, tendu leaves, minerals, scrap)
desc: TCS collected by the seller from the buyer at the time of debiting/receipt, on sale of these specific categories of goods.

variants.condition: Timber obtained under a forest lease
Timber obtained by any other mode (not a forest lease)
Any other forest produce (not timber or tendu leaves)
Minerals — coal, lignite or iron ore (sale to a trader)

notes: Only the liquor and scrap rates actually changed for FY 2026-27 (both 1%→2%); timber/forest-produce rates were separately cut from 2.5% to 2% back in Budget 2025, effective 1 Apr 2025.
Minerals TCS applies only on sale to a trader — not where the buyer uses it for further processing or power generation.
keywords: tcs liquor alcohol timber forest tendu leaves minerals coal lignite iron ore scrap sale

nature: Grant of lease/licence — parking lot, toll plaza, or mining/quarrying rights
desc: TCS on the grant of a lease or licence for a parking lot, toll plaza, or a mine/quarry (other than mineral oil, petroleum and natural gas).
notes: Excludes mining/quarrying of mineral oil, petroleum and natural gas — those are outside this section.
keywords: tcs parking lot toll plaza mining quarrying lease license

nature: Sale of a motor vehicle or notified luxury goods
desc: TCS on high-value sale of a motor vehicle, or of notified luxury goods, to any buyer.

variants.condition: Notified luxury goods (watches, art pieces, yachts, sunglasses, handbags/shoes, home theatre systems, polo horses, etc.)

notes: Luxury-goods list is CBDT-notified and item-specific — check the current notification for what's covered before assuming a category is included.
keywords: tcs motor vehicle car sale luxury watch art yacht bag sunglasses

nature: Remittance under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) / overseas tour packages
desc: TCS collected by an authorised dealer on foreign remittance under LRS, or by a seller of an overseas tour package.

variants.condition: LRS remittance for education or medical treatment
variants.rate: 2% (Nil if funded entirely by an education loan from a specified financial institution)

variants.condition: LRS remittance for any other purpose

variants.rate: 2% up to ₹10 lakh; 5% above ₹10 lakh (if PAN missing or no ITR-filing link)
variants.threshold: No minimum for the base 2% rate

noPan: Twice the applicable rate, or 5%, whichever is higher
notes: Threshold raised from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh by Budget 2025.
The 'other purposes' rate (20%) is a sharp jump from the education/medical rate — classify the purpose carefully before remitting.
keywords: tcs lrs foreign remittance education medical abroad tour package other purpose investment

nature: Sale of goods (general) — WITHDRAWN
desc: Formerly required TCS at 0.1% on sale of goods exceeding ₹50 lakh to one buyer in a year.
notes: Withdrawn with effect from 1 April 2025 — fully subsumed into buyer-side TDS under Sec 194Q (Code 1031).
Kept here for reference only, so a seller doesn't mistakenly try to collect both TCS (old 206C(1H)) and let the buyer also deduct TDS (194Q) on the same sale.
keywords: tcs sale of goods general discontinued withdrawn
